name: bayes_conditioning_audit

direction_isolation_lnBF.meaning: Evidence carried by the R_ML-aligned component of the mass predictor: the log-evidence cost of stripping that direction from the standard model.

nested_aug_vs_raw_standard.meaning: Marginal evidence for adding log R_ML to raw mass+z. Negative: the R_ML direction adds no likelihood beyond the mass+z family under unconditioned predictors.

nested_aug_vs_tep.meaning: Marginal evidence for adding raw mass+z to the single R_ML predictor. Near zero: the theory-fixed predictor recovers essentially all of the augmented model's explanatory power.

conditioning_note: Neither conditioning is neutral. Orthogonalization removes the R_ML-aligned direction from the competitor (TEP-favourable). Raw mass, under the TEP measurement model M_obs = M_true + n*log10 R_ML, contains part of the response itself (standard-favourable). The conditioning-free arbiter is the nested augmented model.

tep_favourable_facts: The R_ML-aligned direction carries essentially all explanatory variance (direction-isolation ln BF = 55.9); the orthogonal complement of mass space is evidentially inert.
The single theory-fixed predictor recovers the full augmented model within ln BF = 18.9 (9 vs 17 parameters).
standard_favourable_facts: The unconditioned mass+z baseline is the single best model (ln BF = -14.4 over TEP-only).
Adding log R_ML to raw mass+z yields ln BF = 4.4 (no marginal gain).
limitations: SED chi^2 is a fit-quality statistic, not a physical observable; the 3-observable physical subset is the primary observable set.
Astrophysical alternatives are parametric stand-ins, not forward-modelled bursty-SF/IMF/AGN predictions; discrimination against realistic physics alternatives is not tested.
Under the TEP measurement model the raw-mass comparison is contaminated (M_obs contains 0.7*log10 R_ML), so the raw result is not a neutral verdict against TEP.
